paper.title: Best arm identification in multi-armed bandits with delayed feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Top-k arm identification (fixed confidence) in sequential MAB with delayed feedback and unbiased noisy partial feedback
unmapped: Each pull has a random arm-specific delay D_s >= 1 during which intermediate partial feedback Y is revealed; the final feedback is sub-Gaussian with mean mu_i and scale sigma_i
Unbiased noisy partial feedback: intermediate observations minus final feedback are independent zero-mean sub-Gaussian with scale sigma_i^(p)
The learner knows the per-arm partial-feedback scale sigma_i^(p)
Only one pull may run at a time; the learner may abandon a running pull; all means are distinct; the k in top-k plays the role of m
settings.definition_quote: Unbiased noisy partial feedback: The partial feedback at the last delay, $Y_{i,t_s+D_s}$ is sub-Gaussian with mean $\mu_i$ and scale parameter $\sigma_i$. For the intermediate time steps, $\Delta \in [1, D_s-1]$, the set of partial feedback $Y_{i,t_s+\Delta}\mid Y_{i,t_s+D_s} - Y_{i,t_s+D_s}$ consists of mutually independent, sub-Gaussian random variables with zero mean and scale parameter $\sigma^{(p)}_{i}$.

conditions: the delay of every arm pull is bounded
the correctness proof only covers the case where the algorithm terminates
tuning: confidence parameter delta is given as input; delta = delta_f + delta_p, with delta_f and delta_p optimised

source.label: thm:seqracingnoisypf_sample
source.quote: Assuming the delay associated with any arm pull is bounded, then Algorithm~\ref{alg:seqracingnoisypf} outputs the top-$k$ arms with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: This is a delta-correctness guarantee (error probability <= delta). The paper does not prove a sample-complexity bound; it only says one could add a D_max factor to the known racing bounds. The proof assumes the algorithm terminates.
